name: Ziza
overview: Ziza was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Rehoboam and Maacah. His identity is grounded in his lineage, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 11:20, with no additional biblical notes elaborating on his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Ziza is a proper name and is described as a childish abbreviation, similar to a name of endearment like 'mama.' It was not given by God but appears as a personal name in Scripture (2 Chronicles 11:20).
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ziza as the son of Rehoboam and Maacah, establishing his direct royal lineage. No other family relationships beyond these parents are noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ziza's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily tied to his heritage as a son of Rehoboam, the king of Judah, and Maacah. This connection places him within the Davidic royal line, emphasizing the continuation of Judah's royal family. While the Bible does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his mention preserves the genealogical record important for understanding the lineage of Judah's kings.
